[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of attention head specialization in MoE transformers via information-theoretic or mechanistic interpretability frameworks (e.g., analyzing mutual information between head routing and causal variables) — Formalizing 'modular specialization' as a constraint on the capacity of individual heads and deriving conditions under which such specialization leads to learning of invariant causal mechanisms (e.g., via the principle of independent mechanisms) would provide a rigorous foundation to confirm or refute the hypothesis.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of existing empirical studies on out-of-distribution robustness and causal representation learning in mixture-of-experts transformers (e.g., works on MoE for compositional generalization or domain adaptation) — Surveying current evidence from papers on MoE attention (e.g., Switch Transformer, Mixtral) and causal representation learning (e.g., causal abstraction, interchange interventions) can reveal whether modular specialization correlates with improved causal invariance or if counterexamples exist.
